WTI ~101. Intraday path was worse than the settle (morning quotes ~114.3-115.2) — selling accelerated into the close. Leg fails only on a settle below the 104.72 firing floor; tonight's settle is the next print.

**Fed — FOMC DAY 1; the December dislocation is ADJUDICATED, resolved against futures.** Statement tomorrow Oct-28 14:00 ET, Warsh presser 14:30. Fresh direct CME print via Yahoo Finance (S, Oct-26): October hold **90.6%** (firmed from the 84.0 CME print at T-7), December hike **72.1%**. The pre-committed rule from the 2026-10-26 watch: 'a fresh direct CME print inside 5pts of the prediction-market relay (76-77) reverses the lean.' 72.1 lands 3.9-4.9pts under the relay — CONDITION MET. The widest tracked dislocation (13-18pt at its peak) collapsed with CME converging to the books, not the reverse: the 'futures know better' lean was WRONG, the prediction-market relay was right. Logged as a resolved dislocation; the venue-spread watch item closes here unless a fresh divergence re-opens post-statement. September CPI 3.7% remains the hawk's case, the 29k payroll the dove's; PCE lands Thursday morning, the day after the statement.

**Hormuz — the weekend was NOT quiet: self-catch #2.** Last cycle logged 'no searchable escalation headline — weekend gap-risk UNFIRED' and 'first quiet weekend.' Monday's press record contradicts the factual half: Houthi forces claimed attacks on a Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday, and Saudi authorities reported intercepting additional missiles and drones on Sunday (Angel One, B, Oct-26). The price-outcome half survived — Brent eased rather than gapped — but 'quiet weekend' is WITHDRAWN. Overnight: gCaptain reports a tanker disabled in the strait and a separate vessel on fire in the Gulf — single-source, unconfirmed; an IRGC-affiliated claim via Saba declares the strait 'completely closed' (state-affiliated claim, not established fact); Iran claims the strait could reopen in four to five days if conditions are met (bloomingbit relay, uncorroborated); INTERTANKO says transits on the US-backed route exceed 30/day vs PortWatch's 4/day AIS count (Oct-18) — the claim-vs-confirmation five-way persists, now with a transit-count split layered on top. straits.live showed Brent spot 115.22 at 20:59 UTC Monday vs the 110.27 settle — tape fracture between spot trackers and the futures tape, logged.

**Riyadh — owed adjudication RESOLVED: the Oct-24 marker became extensions, not resumptions.** Etihad and Qatar Airways did not resume after their 'through Oct-24' windows; the carrier ledger now reads: Lufthansa RUH suspended through Nov-18 (Dammam Nov-30), KLM RUH/DMM through Oct-31, Philippine Airlines through Nov-29, Cathay postponed to end-Jan-2027, Delta ATL-RUH launch to Mar-2027, British Airways restart planned Nov-3. The airport remains technically open under GACA prior-permission NOTAMs A3650/26 and A3651/26 with no expiry; only Saudia and flynas listed as operating. Two consecutive owed adjudications now settle to one dated ledger. Next markers: KLM Oct-31 (4 days), BA Nov-3 (7 days, midterm day), Lufthansa Nov-18. Separate flag: the Houthi Saturday claim targeted 'the Saudi airport' — outlet did not name which; RUH-specific claim count stays at zero.
